title: Measurement
description: Class 4 IMO — Measurement: converting length (km, m, cm), weight (kg, g) and capacity (L, mL), working with mixed units, and solving real-life word problems.

topics.title: Length Conversions (km, m, cm)
topics.concept:
Length uses kilometres (km), metres (m) and centimetres (cm), with 1 km = 1000 m and 1 m = 100 cm.

To change a bigger unit to a smaller one, multiply (3 km = 3000 m); to change a smaller unit to a bigger one, divide (400 cm = 4 m).

examples.problem: Change 250 cm into metres and centimetres.

recap: Bigger to smaller: multiply. Smaller to bigger: divide.

topics.title: Weight (kg, g) & Capacity (L, mL)
topics.concept:
Weight uses kilograms (kg) and grams (g) with 1 kg = 1000 g. Capacity uses litres (L) and millilitres (mL) with 1 L = 1000 mL.

A mixed measure like 2 kg 500 g equals 2500 g, and 1500 mL equals 1 L 500 mL.
recap: Combine the parts: 2 kg 500 g = 2500 g.

quiz.explanation: 1000 mL = 1 L, plus 500 mL, so 1 L 500 mL.

topics.title: Mixed Units & Word Problems
topics.concept:
To add or subtract mixed units, work on each unit separately, regrouping when needed. For 2 m 50 cm + 1 m 30 cm, add metres and centimetres to get 3 m 80 cm.

In word problems, convert to the same unit if necessary, then add or subtract.
recap: Add/subtract each unit separately, regrouping if needed.
Convert to the same unit when the problem mixes units.

questions.q: Which is the odd one out (three measure length)?
questions.explanation: kg measures weight; the others measure length.

questions.q: Which is longer, 1 km or 999 m?
questions.explanation: 1 km = 1000 m, which is more than 999 m.

questions.q: A rope is 5 m long. A piece of 2 m 50 cm is cut off. How much is left?
A bag has 3 kg 500 g of rice. 1 kg 500 g more is added. How much rice now?
A tank holds 10 L. 6 L 500 mL is used. How much is left?
Sara walks 2 km 300 m, then 1 km 800 m more. How far in all?
1 kg of sugar is shared equally into 4 packets. How much is in each packet?
